generation.explanation: With 100% annual interest compounded n times per year, your $1 becomes (1 + 1/n)ⁿ after one year: yearly compounding gives $2.00, monthly gives about $2.61, and daily gives about $2.7146. The surprise is that this doesn't blow up — it converges to a finite limit, e ≈ 2.71828, which is exactly what continuous compounding yields. The graph plots your final balance against n on a logarithmic scale, so you can drag the yellow dot (or slider) from n = 1 to n = 1000 and watch the value lock onto the horizontal line at e.
